findings.text: the published snapshot's per-session payload extends only sub-floor, held-worktree and unreadable-record items, so the index-lag notice added at reckon/crew/obligations.py:2946 never reaches the prompt-path checklist the hook reads; a session sees it only through the MCP/CLI obligations view or the inline stop derivation, so the hook's new index-lags-head vocabulary entry is unexercised on the snapshot path.

_read_only_git duplicates reckon/velocity.py:163 run_git rather than extending it: the git -C argv, byte capture, check=False and 180 s timeout are identical, and the only addition is GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, which belongs on the owner as an env parameter so the capability keeps one implementation.

the assertion compares the log record's head with the notice row's head, and both are produced by the same _index_lag_paths call, so a detector that reported a wrong HEAD would satisfy it; comparing against the checkout's own git rev-parse HEAD would make it independent.

item_verdicts.diff: read all four commits against bb23ab6e: obligations.py adds the detector, notice and log; the hook mirrors the non-blocking kind; the test file adds five cases; the evidence fragment records the landing.
